 Microsoft Kicks Off Xbox 25th Anniversary Celebrations
 News 
 Xbox 
 Jon "Sikamikanico" Clarke 
 9 hours ago
 Become a Member
 Join Now! 
 Xbox CEO Asha Sharma has kicked off today’s 25th Anniversary celebrations with a new blog post over on Xbox Wire. 
 In a message sent to all staff at Team Xbox, Sharma recounted the journey for Microsoft through video games, from the early days of Microsoft Adventure in 1979, to the very first Flight Simulator, and such classics like Minesweeper and Age of Empires.
 Of course, all of this effort culminated in the first iteration of DirectX, and then the original Xbox in 2001. It’s fair to say that the original Xbox, and through multiplayer networks like Xbox Live, revolutionized online gaming on console, and the rest as they say, is history. 
As for the next 25 years, it’s fair to say that Microsoft faces a significant challenge. The Xbox brand has never been in a more precarious position, so fans are assuredly eager to know more about what’s next for the Xbox brand. Here’s what Asha had to say:
 Gaming has always been an industry driven by dreams. Not just the desire to bring something imagined to life, but to share it with others. Sometimes that dream is of a game, other times a console, a character, or an entire universe. The history of XBOX is a testament to the power of these dreams and how they can grow over time.   
 The first Microsoft Flight Simulator was just 160 KB, with 2D graphics, 16 colors, and 20 total airports. The 2024 version draws on more than 2.5 petabytes of data (more than 15 billion times the size of the original game). Its 200-million-square-mile map recreates almost every city, road, and landmark across the planet, with trillions of individually rendered trees and real-world weather reproduced in near real time. 
 While modern games demonstrate the heights of human craft in ways unimaginable just decades ago, the cost, resources, and risk required to create them have grown just as dramatically. As a result, too many ideas never become games, and too many games fall short of what their creators imagined. For decades, this has been the unavoidable tradeoff of ambition. We must change this. 
 Throughout human history, the scale of what we could create was determined by the people, capital, and resources we could command. That relationship is beginning to break. A single person will soon be able to wield capabilities that once required entire nations. A small team will be able to build worlds that today demand hundreds of developers and hundreds of millions of dollars. And our largest studios will be able to pursue ambitions as far beyond today’s games as Microsoft Flight Simulator 2024 is from its first entry in 1982. 
 I believe the future of gaming will look more like its beginning, when a small team with a big idea could change how the world plays. Our responsibility is to deliver great games, unmistakable hardware, and give more people the chance to make something the world has never seen. 
 Happy Birthday XBOX! 
 Xbox CEO Asha Sharma via Xbox Wire.
